## Song · fx.01
**Title:** The Tree of the Body
**Summary:** TEST FIXTURE. The body is pictured as a tree with five branches, and the poet urges the listener to steady great bliss by asking the guru. Munidatta reads the five branches as the five aggregates.
> Questions from the drafter:
> - Keep 'tree' for taruvara, or 'fine tree'?
**Decision:**
**Note to next draft:**

## 1.1 · fx.01.1
> (refrain)
> কাআ তরুবর পঞ্চ বি ডাল।   kāā tarubara pañca bi ḍāla|
> *body · fine-tree · five · also · branch*
> চঞ্চল চীএ পইঠো কাল॥ ধ্রু॥   cañcala cīe paiṭho kāla|| dhru||
> drafter's transliteration: cañcala cīe paiṭho kāla
> *restless · in-mind · entered · time*
**EN 1a:** The body is a fine [tree]{taruvara} with five branches;
**EN 1b:** into the restless mind, time has entered.
**Note 1 · doctrine · cites fx.01.m1:** Munidatta reads the five branches of the tree as the five aggregates.
**Note 2 · philology:** The refrain couplet; ধ্রু marks it for repetition.
> FLAG 1b · meaning · medium: kāla may be 'time' or 'death'; I chose time.
**Decision:**
**Note to next draft:**

## Munidatta on 1.1 · fx.01.m1
> কায়স্তরুবরঃ পঞ্চবিডালঃ ইতি পঞ্চস্কন্ধাঃ।
> kāyastaruvaraḥ pañcaviḍālaḥ iti pañcaskandhāḥ
> Equations: পঞ্চবিডালঃ = the five aggregates (taruvara)
**Translation:** The body is the fine [tree]{taruvara}; its five branches are the five aggregates.
**Note:** Munidatta reads the five branches of the body-tree as the five aggregates.
**Decision:**

## 1.2 · fx.01.2
> (bhaṇitā: the poet names himself)
> দিঢ় করিঅ মহাসুহ পরিমাণ।   diṛha karia mahāsuha parimāṇa|
> *firm · having-made · great-bliss · measure*
> লুই ভণই গুরু পুচ্ছিঅ জাণ॥   lui bhaṇai guru pucchia jāṇa||
> *Lūyī · says · guru · having-asked · know*
**EN 2a:** Make [great bliss]{mahasukha} firm and take its measure:
**EN 2b:** [Lūyī]{p-luyi} says: ask the guru, and know.
